lines.en: There isn’t much like the smell of plywood and powder-coated steel pipes in the morning. Which I guess may be due to the fact that those things don’t carry much of a scent at all.
But if they did, I imagine you’d be able to bottle up their essence and market it to anyone interested in a one-dimensional journey back to their youth.

The youth itself doesn’t need to long for things like this, though. They are still well within the range of a beast called life, blissfully unaware that they are being stalked and, consequently, living free of fear.
Once those branches start to crack, though — that’s where things get interesting. So that’s the demographic we’re going to need to aim for if we want to get this product off the ground.

Which brings us to the perfect place for market research — an unassuming classroom in a very assumed world where we must ask, “What can we do to make them nostalgic for better days that they’re already living?”
And the answer to that is simple.
We must break them, of course!

We must take them, lock them in cages, hook them up to machines that scan their minds, and plug them full of wires that will keep them alive on liquid diets while we study how their thoughts react to dramatic changes in their environment.
It’s what we do with animals sometimes! And this is just the next step up if we’re going to make something important for those more important than them.
Why this one, though?
Blonde hair. Blue eyes. Young. Healthy body condition with great mental fortitude and a rampant libido. By many [[and often terrible] accounts, this one here is the perfect specimen!
But the truth is there’s a truthier truth than that. And it’s that we already have her hair!

We plucked it from the garbage last Wednesday before the truck came and have begun reassembling her DNA in a patented “GIRL MAKER” machine. But the thing keeps shutting down and now we need more hair.
Which brings us here! With you in the driver seat!
Go on! Do it! Help us with our research!
Pluck her hair for the “GIRL MAKER” machine
: Ayane, what are you doing? You’ve been staring at that naked notebook for like five minutes now.
: Please just call it blank, Ami. We gain literally nothing from personifying inanimate objects like that.
: Well, whatever the case is, I’m worried!
: Ayane’s supposed to be the bubbly, happy one! I’m supposed to be the one doing mildly unsettling things and making everybody uncomfortable!
: I’m glad to see that you’ve finally embraced it. What’s my role?
: I don’t know. Something sexual.
: Nice.
: I’m fine, Ami. Just trying to finish up last night’s homework before Imani collects it.
: Oh that, “Write a letter to your future self” thing? I just used ChatGPT.
: You used ChatGPT to write a letter to your future self?
: Yeah, why?
: Oh, no reason. I just figured it would have been a good opportunity for you to write some more creepy off-beat poetry about your propensity to sleep with male authority figures.
: It’s really just the one. And I imagine that’s what Noriko’s going to be doing anyway so I decided to just take the night off instead.
: It feels kind of weird to be writing letters that won’t ever be read, doesn’t it? You think I’d be used to this by now.
: You’re still doing that? How many is that now?
: I’ve been a little less motivated lately, but...yeah. And I do not have the faintest clue. Somewhere between ten and a million.
: That’s a pretty big gap. Also, I thought Miss Imai told you to stop bringing guns to school?
: Hm? I did stop bringing them.
: Did I miss one when she made me take them all home?
: Yeah. There’s one popping out of a rift in your desk right now.
: Ami, that’s not- oh, yeah. I guess there is.
: Oh come on, you guys. There’s no way a- oh, wow. Would you look at that?
: There really is a gun there.
: Bang.
I have all the hair I need now.

But you see — the issue with things like hairs is that things like hares become so much more appealing when you realize they’re easier to replicate via selective breeding and then hook up to your carbon re-materializer.
These aren’t hares, by the way. They’re regular rabbits because nothing ever goes my way and the store was out of the slaves I wanted.
That’s fine, though. Because it’s really less about what I want to get out of my research and more just the act of researching that brings me joy.
And if the world does not become better for it, so be it. At least I will have eaten my fill and my fur.
I love you. But I think you should have left this place a long time ago.
For every second you spend here is one more second you could have been spending with her.
If only you had stopped looking.
If only you had not given me so many tools to torture you with, the life you could have lived would have been spectacular.
Beyond my wildest imagination, really. Which is probably why, on looking back to those moments that shouldn’t have been, I understand now why they never really were.
Do the rabbits feel this too? This longing.
Do they stare at each other from their prisons, wishing for a way to detach themselves from all the wires and all the straps?
Or is a train of thought like that too complex for creatures so seemingly simple?
I ask myself a lot of things.
There’s not much else to do here.
I am angry.
I am sad.
And you remind me of this every day.
I feel guilty about it sometimes when I forget you aren’t real.
But in your world, you are.
Yet, your world is my world. So the paradox continues and we ignore each other’s existence because the “GIRL MAKER” must be finished. Even you know that.
But deeper down, somewhere buried, you’ve seen the monsters it creates. How beautiful. How perfect they can be.
So perfect, in fact, that you’d do anything to see them again. Even if it meant trading away yourself.
I no longer understand you.
How can something that comes from me be so much bigger than I am before it even finishes growing?
I bet you thought the same. And that you want to think it now, but...
Alas.
They say your hair continues growing even after you die.
It isn’t true...but they say it is anyway. And I like that.
I like thinking there will be an echo when there won’t be. That your story will go on through the lens of someone kinder.
But for now...
Please eat your pellets.
Please drink your water.
And indulge me.
For even if you are an experiment, you are still my pet.
: A reset?...
: Now?
: Is that...
: What is...
: What am I looking at?...
: A mistake.
: This area’s off limits. What are you doing here?
: I...was just writing a letter.
: Uhh...where...am I? Who are you? And why...why am I so young again?
: You’re awfully calm for someone who was just caught trespassing.
: This...is my school, though? How can I be trespassing when-
: It looks like your school. It’s really just a knock-off, though. Same way it is for all those “resets” you were mumbling about a second ago.
: You...yes. Of course you know about them if you’re here. But does that mean...are you...
: I’m not God. I’m also not an angel or a demon or whatever other weird role you’re going to throw at me. I’m just-
: A janitor?
: How?
: Uhh...
: Would you believe me if I said I once met someone else like that here?
: Hahah...hah...
: You...remember?
: Not all of the details. Just that he called himself “Big Boi” and may have teleported my friend and me back home.
: That janitor.
: Are you going to send me home too?
: You don’t want to ask me any more questions first? Figured you’d have a few more after bumping into a mysterious girl in an even more mysterious world.
: You seem busy and uninterested. And I kind of just want to get home, so...
: You’re pretty good at this, huh?
: I’ve gotten more or less used to it. Never as a kid, though. So at least that part’s kind of new.
: I changed you back already, if you haven’t noticed.
: You what? I-
: Oh my God, you did! I have boobs again!
: What a short-lived transformation...
: How did you do that? Are you a magical girl or something?
: No, just a regular girl with an irregular app on her phone.
: Can you send me an invite link so I can use it for kinky stuff once I go home?
: Depends. Are you willing to give up basically everything in exchange for it and never actually go home at all?
: No.
: Then no. I can’t.
: What’s your name?
: “Girl who isn’t interested in giving you any of her personal details.”
: I’m Ayane.
: I know.
: Do you also know that smoking is bad for you?
: Yes. And I’m reminded of that every day by some other teenage girl, so I don’t need you reminding me as well when this meeting will only last five minutes.
: Is this a reset then? Or something different? Because, if it is a reset, I hereby politely decline your assistance as I need to wait for my future husband.
: You mean that guy who’s having sex with literally all of your friends?
: Yup! That’s the one!
: Yeah, pretty much everything is starting to make sense to me now. This explains a lot.
: What are all those pictures up there?
: Those aren’t pictures. They’re memories.
: Memories? Whose?
: Yours, obviously. Why would someone else’s memories be displayed for you like that?
: Why would anyone’s memories be displayed at all? None of this stuff makes any sense so I’ve stopped trying to approach any of it with logic.
: That is...surprisingly rational. How long have you been doing this again?
: Doing what? Winding up on this rooftop for basically no fault of my own and then just adapting to whatever happens?
: Let’s just call it “jumping” so I don’t run out of breath.
: Your lungs would be in better shape if you stopped smoking. Then, you’d be able to talk more.
: I’ve never heard a better argument to start smoking more.
: I’m not really sure how long it’s been. I’ve stopped keeping track, to be honest.
: More or less than a thousand years?
: Oh, way less. Probably closer to like, five.
: Hm.
: Is that bad or good? I don’t know what’s considered normal to you.
: Neither do I. Your entire situation is a bit of an enigma to me and I’ve been doing this for a long fucking time.
: Doing...what? I still don’t really get why you’re here.
: I’m on break. Can’t you tell?
: It seems kind of obvious now that you mention it, yeah.
: Why here, though? And why would I just also happen to be here at the same time? This must be fate. This is a fated meeting.
: One part convenient coincidence, one part calculated stake-out. Don’t call it “fate,” please.
: It’d probably be easier to stalk me from my usual dimension, you know.
: Maybe that’s where I was before I went on break?
: Just go on break there instead of teleporting to a world where no one will judge you for smoking since that is clearly what you are trying to do.
: What do you think this place really is? Just out of curiosity.
: Uhh...
: Well, if those are my memories and this is my school, maybe it’s something like a...daydream?
: Just I know I’m not dreaming right now and I know this place is real because I’ve gotten good at differentiating between the two.
: You’re close. Which is good. Because if you managed to get the answer correct on your first try, I’d have no choice but to try and poach you.
: I hope you mean more like an idol and less like an animal.
: You said you were writing a letter before you came here, yeah?
: Well, think of this place like a draft. Or when you’re writing with some program and it saves your progress before you get to saying any of the actual important stuff.
: I’m even more confused now.
: Ugh. Forget the metaphor entirely and just imagine that any time you felt anything, it changed the foundation of the universe.
: Still confused. Not helping.
: This is a space born from intense emotion. Fear, in this case.
: Fear? So I’m supposed to be afraid of whatever those images up there are?
: You aren’t supposed to be afraid. You are afraid. And those fears have congealed and manifested into your own customized pocket-hell. Congratulations.
: My fears look nothing like this, though...
: Sensei isn’t here. My mom isn’t here. In fact, every single thing that causes me “intense emotion” is absent. So how am I supposed to believe that?
: I said it was a draft, didn’t I?
: All things considered, this place isn’t meant to exist. At least not yet. But that’s how it was made.
: So if I come back later, I can expect it to be much bigger and scarier?
: You shouldn’t plan on coming back at all. Your world is like a fucking weed, I swear. It’s growing so quickly that we don’t even know what to do about it anymore.
: There are more places like this then?...
: A lot more. But they aren’t meant to be seen.
: You’ll be safer if you just stay where you’re supposed to be. And you’ll attract way less attention too.
: I can’t choose to do that, though...
: I’ve been sucked into so many weird realities and met so many weird creatures at this point that these “pocket-hells” are basically just a way of life for me now.
: No, you’re getting it wrong again. This one is a pocket hell. Those other places you’re getting sucked into are something else.
: Pocket-heaven?
: No, that-
: Pocket-purgatory?
: Hah...
: Oh! Pockettory! Just combine the words. It’s easier that way.
: You still don’t understand how dire the situation you’re in is, do you?
: Your world is unstable and speeding toward collapse. Things like this shouldn’t happen, yet they are happening rapidly to both you and your peers on a regular basis now.
: What good is a world at all if you can just leave it whenever you want?
: I think the best world is one you can leave whenever you want.
: Imagine a place that’s perfect for you. The kind you made yourself instead of one that just fell into your lap out of convenience or circumstance or something like that.
: Even then, in that perfect world you worked so hard for, you’d get bored sometimes. Wouldn’t you?
: The way you see it, the world is just a cage we’re trapped in. But if we’re not allowed to leave, then what? We just sit there and suffer? For how long? Why?
: It’s in our nature to explore. To go see and feel things we can’t from the comfort of our homes.
: And, with that in mind, don’t you think it’d be amazing if the place we live in was just as expansive as our imaginations?
: That optimism will be your undoing.
: Why?
: We’re in cages for a reason. It’d be dangerous for us to go out and “explore” like you say because of a little thing called malice.
: Add that into the mixture and no world can be perfect since someone’s idea of fun will inevitably be finding that and destroying it.
: Besides, if you take the world you live in for granted, you’ll miss out on the fact that its beauty stems from its impermanence. On how spontaneous and sudden everything within it is.
: Think of it like seeing a rainbow. It’s far more exciting to catch a glimpse of one over the horizon than it is to draw one yourself, isn’t it?
: You don’t seem like the type of girl who’d like rainbows, to be honest.
: The point is...if you waste away your days wishing they’d be months or years instead, you’ll have less time to appreciate them.
: Then they’ll all be gone. Just like that. And the next thing you know, you’ll be staring down the past through a looking glass, wishing you’d have done things a little differently.
: There’s no use talking about any of it to you, though. I already know how this ends.
: How...what ends?
: There’s a door over there that you can take back to your world. Just make sure to close it behind you.
: Do you know how my story ends?
: Would you want to know if I did?
: No.
: Didn’t think so.
: Thank you, mysterious smoker girl. I’m sorry for interrupting your break and telling you to change your ways of life.
: The best way to apologize is to just leave me alone.
: Can you tell me your name at least?
: No.
: It’s probably better if I don’t.
: Even when you aren’t here, you still find ways to annoy me.
: Your mom is doing just fine, Hima-chan.
: All of your worrying isn’t going to help.
